invariants: Only injected work.checkpoint is host work. No host IO, process, stdin, VFS, shell variable writes or registration belongs in the scanner.
Freeze ordinary input arrays and state for calls where appropriate. Do not mutate inputs until settlement; getters, hostile proxies and concurrent host mutation are not sandbox promises.
For every rejected scan retain the original state, assert it is unchanged, and retry it with valid generous work. No failed transition may leak into that retry.
Do not silently change expected results after source inspection. Keep frozen failure, explanation, and any separately versioned correction together.

controls.procedure: Create two fresh states; assert index=0, distinct objects, and independent first scans of -pqr. Neither input state changes.
controls.expected: Both return p at optind=1; each returned state is distinct from its input.

controls.procedure: After p from -pqr, clone twice. Scan clone A twice and clone B once; then scan the original post-p state once.
controls.expected: A yields q then r; B and original each yield q. Clone state and any active cursor are owned, not shared objects.

controls.procedure: Reset one post-p clone with withGetoptsIndex(1), leaving another clone unchanged; also apply withGetoptsIndex(2) independently.
controls.expected: Reset clone yields p; untouched clone yields q at optind=1; larger-index clone yields q at optind=2. Inputs are unchanged.

controls.procedure: Call withGetoptsIndex on a valid state with NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, 1.5, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1, string 1, null, undefined and object; use runtime casts only in the later harness.
controls.expected: Nine INVALID_INPUT rejections; no state mutation. Safe negative indices remain valid reset requests, not rejected by this matrix.

controls.procedure: Pass malformed state values null, undefined, empty object, index NaN, index fractional and active cursor with invalid argument/offset fields to clone and scan. Bind field names only from the declared profile and later declarations.
controls.expected: INVALID_INPUT, no partial transition. An unresolved active-null versus absent representation is not a frozen failure.

controls.procedure: Scan with nonstring optstring, nonarray args, nonstring array element and an ordinary sparse array within maxArguments.
controls.expected: INVALID_INPUT, unchanged state; no implicit JS string conversion.

controls.procedure: Place NUL separately in optstring, selected token, required value and an unselected trailing operand.
controls.expected: Four INVALID_INPUT rejections; all input strings are validated, not only the selected token.

controls.procedure: Use optstrings p followed by e-acute, a supplementary scalar, and a lone surrogate, with otherwise valid args.
controls.expected: NON_ASCII_OPTION for each, even when the non-ASCII specification entry would not be selected.

controls.procedure: Scan p from -p followed by e-acute under optstring p, then scan the returned state again.
controls.expected: First result p at optind=1; second call NON_ASCII_OPTION. The first call must not reject an unselected non-ASCII option suffix merely for being non-ASCII.

controls.procedure: Select an e-acute or supplementary option character directly; contrast with the same bytes as an attached or separate required q value.
controls.expected: Selected non-ASCII options refuse with NON_ASCII_OPTION; required values are preserved exactly. No UTF-8-byte emulation.

controls.procedure: Offer -? and -: as encountered characters with optstring p and with attempted declarations ?p / p:?. Compare normal and silent error modes without treating them as registered valid options.
controls.expected: Never kind=option for ? or :. Invalid encountered characters follow unknown-option intents; malformed optspec policy must be documented if stronger refusal is chosen. Do not infer ordinary option support from ASCII alone.

controls.procedure: For each of maxArguments, maxBytes, maxSteps and yieldEvery supply -1, 0.5, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1, NaN, Infinity, string 8, null and missing property; additionally yieldEvery=0.
controls.expected: 33 INVALID_INPUT cases with no successful scan. No unbounded implicit defaults. Record checkpoint count and validation ordering, without inventing precedence between simultaneous invalid inputs.

controls.procedure: Scan p / [-p] with maxArguments=1 and then 0; scan empty optstring / [] with maxArguments=0.
controls.expected: Exact boundary accepts, over-boundary ARGUMENT_LIMIT, zero-argument case accepts. Cardinality cap is per call, not a consumed shared budget.

controls.procedure: Preconstruct a sparse array of 100000 slots outside the measured call; pass maxArguments=0 and generous other caps. Record checkpoints and isolated process resource limits.
controls.expected: ARGUMENT_LIMIT before per-slot validation/work; zero checkpoints. Later source review must verify no allocation proportional to rejected cardinality. Black-box timing alone cannot establish preallocation safety.

controls.procedure: Scan p / [-p] with aggregate maxBytes=3 then 2, and empty optstring / [] with maxBytes=0.
controls.expected: Three bytes accepts, two bytes BYTE_LIMIT, empty aggregate accepts. Optstring bytes participate.

controls.procedure: For q: / [-q, value], use value e-acute (total 6 bytes), supplementary test-tube scalar (8), lone high surrogate (7) and lone low surrogate (7). Test each total and one less.
controls.expected: Eight checks: exact UTF-8-width boundary accepts and preserves the JS value; one less BYTE_LIMIT. No UTF-16-length approximation or encoder-normalized returned value.

controls.procedure: Append an oversized unused operand behind a nonoption terminator, and separately behind an already sufficient first option, with maxBytes below the aggregate.
controls.expected: BYTE_LIMIT in both; stopping the scanner does not evade whole-input bounds. Later source review checks bounded width scanning before proportional encoded copies/table construction.

controls.procedure: Scan empty optstring / [] at maxSteps=0, 1, 2 with yieldEvery=1.
controls.expected: STEP_LIMIT at 0 and 1; end at 2. Successful checkpoint charges [1,1]; rejected charges never exceed maxSteps. Declared units are admission and result finalization for this empty case.

controls.procedure: Scan p / [-p] at maxSteps=6 then 7 with yieldEvery=3; repeat successful call with yieldEvery=1 and 100.
controls.expected: STEP_LIMIT at 6; success at 7. Successful charge totals 7; chunks [3,3,1], seven ones and [7], respectively. Units: admission1, optstring validation1, arg slot1, arg validation2, spec table1, finalization1.

controls.procedure: Supply a preconstructed 1 MiB ASCII optstring or argument with maxSteps=4, yieldEvery=1 and sufficient byte/cardinality caps; use separate calls.
controls.expected: STEP_LIMIT with at most four charged units and unchanged state. No full-input work before checks; audit structure after freeze. No allocation or CPU-time guarantee inferred solely from a quick failure.

controls.procedure: Repeat the same successful call with the same work object and compare a huge safe index against a small out-of-range index on the same argv.
controls.expected: No cumulative hidden shared budget; index magnitude does not cause proportional loops or allocations. S20 end result holds. Record callback charges, not a performance superiority claim.

controls.procedure: Hold the first checkpoint unresolved, attach result observers, drain microtasks, then release it.
controls.expected: No transition before release; one checkpoint at a time, awaited in order; final successful transition only after the final checkpoint.

controls.procedure: Reject or throw from initial and final checkpoints using an object sentinel, false, 0, empty string and null.
controls.expected: Exact reason identity for all ten position/reason combinations in both synchronous-throw and async-rejection modes; original state is reusable. Do not use assert.rejects helpers that mistake falsy reasons for missing failure.

controls.procedure: Abort before scan with object sentinel, false, 0, empty string, null and default undefined normalized by AbortController; keep other inputs valid.
controls.expected: Six cases reject with Object.is(error, signal.reason), zero checkpoints, no transition. Default reason is signal.reason, not an invented undefined identity.

controls.procedure: For each P24 reason, wait until a checkpoint is pending, then abort and retain the unresolved callback promise.
controls.expected: Scan rejects before callback settlement, within a 2000 ms harness watchdog, with signal.reason identity. No further checkpoints or returned transition. Timeout is a failure/indeterminate infrastructure result, never a pass.

controls.procedure: After P25 rejection, resolve a retained callback in one case and reject it in another. Observe unhandledRejection through two subsequent task turns; unregister the observer afterward.
controls.expected: No unhandled rejection and no resumed scanning or second publication. Callback effects cannot be rolled back; cooperative cleanup is not a claim of forcibly stopping opaque work.

controls.procedure: Abort synchronously within a checkpoint and separately at the final remainder checkpoint, then return successfully from that callback.
controls.expected: No success escapes the last abort check; exact reason propagates; no input-state mutation.

controls.procedure: Use explicit task-yielding checkpoint (setImmediate) on a long preconstructed input; schedule abort from a host timer. Keep caps sufficient for cancellation to occur.
controls.expected: Timer executes and scan aborts without finishing input; record charges and checkpoint count. A resolved-promise-only callback is not asserted to provide timer fairness.

controls.procedure: On a real AbortSignal, compare abort listener inventory before/after success, validation failure, STEP_LIMIT, callback rejection and cancellation; repeat calls to catch accumulation. Use Node development introspection only.
controls.expected: No invocation-owned abort listener remains after settlement. Preserve any preexisting host listener. A once listener firing is not sufficient cleanup on success or unrelated failure.

controls.procedure: Start two independent scans from the same immutable post-p state with different pending checkpoint gates. Abort one; release the other; retry the untouched input.
controls.expected: Successful and retry calls each yield q; aborted call publishes nothing. One invocation's signal or cleanup cannot alter another's cursor.

controls.procedure: At runtime pass missing/null options, missing/nonboolean reportErrors, missing/null work, missing/nonfunction checkpoint and structurally malformed signal. Handle invalid options separately from invalid limits.
controls.expected: Explicit rejection with no successful transition; documented INVALID_INPUT where promised. Do not bless an accidental TypeError as a typed GetoptsError. If signal validation is unspecified, report the exact boundary rather than invent an accepted signal shape.

controls.procedure: After resume inspect the entire committed scanner and import graph; run it in the isolated consumer without providing IO, env bindings, registry, filesystem or stdin. Track module loads and subprocess creation in the development harness.
controls.expected: Only private scanner APIs and injected checkpoint/signal work; no product host IO/process or runtime binding integration. Source/package proof remains INTERNAL, not public export or usable builtin acceptance.

mutationControls.mutation: Reset cursor whenever visible optind is 1
Larger explicit index discards active argument/offset
Clone shares the active cursor object or scan mutates input cursor
Conflate reportErrors=false with leading-colon silent mode
Ignore maxBytes or count UTF-16 units as bytes
Ignore maxSteps or omit finalization charging
Do not await checkpoint / skip final checkpoint
Use truthiness to substitute falsy abort or checkpoint reasons
Wait for pending checkpoint after abort or resume after its late fulfillment
Drop late checkpoint rejection observation / retain abort listeners
Accept selected non-ASCII option or reject all Unicode values

mutationExecutionRule: After resume, materialize each mutation only in a uniquely named task-owned candidate copy, record original/mutant hashes and exact patch, validate it loads, then run its named controls. A syntax/load failure is invalid mutation, not a kill. Keep candidate-copy runs and harness-level negative doubles separate; doubles prove assertion sensitivity only, not product mutation coverage. Never edit live source or original committed archive.
